name: Bamanbore–Nagpur Highway
aka: Formed from the former NH 8A (part), NH 59, NH 59A and NH 69 (part)
history: NH 47 runs across the middle of India, from Bamanbore in Gujarat's Saurashtra region to Nagpur in Maharashtra. On the way it connects two of western and central India's biggest cities, Ahmedabad and Indore. It was pieced together in the 2010 renumbering from four older highways, including the busy old NH 59 between Ahmedabad and Indore.
facts: Crosses three states: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.
Made from the old highways NH 8A (in part), NH 59, NH 59A and NH 69 (in part).
Passes through Multai, the town where the Tapti river begins.
Meets NH 27 at Bamanbore and NH 44 near Nagpur.
